rule: Every finding has an id, owner and status. No finding is left unowned. Status reflects LIVE code/CI, not prior reports.

findings.source_report: OWNER directive Wave D + LAW 10 (ERROR SEMANTICS != TEXT SEARCH)
findings.precondition: FallbackProvider wraps any primary whose generate() returns model text, or raises an exception whose str() happens to contain '429'/'quota'/'rate limit'/'daily limit'.
findings.failure_scenario: A legitimate, successful model answer that merely mentions HTTP 429 / quota / rate-limit is substring-matched and wrongly discarded; the user is silently degraded to the FakeLLM fallback. Conversely, an unrelated exception whose text contains '429' is swallowed into fallback instead of propagating (fail-open).
findings.root_cause: Provider failure was classified by free-form TEXT search on (a) the primary's returned model output and (b) str(exception), instead of by typed exception + status. Model text and provider errors were conflated.
findings.fix: Introduced typed LLMError(kind,status) in src/nexus_ai_agent/llm/errors.py; FallbackProvider now returns any normally-returned non-empty string verbatim (success) and degrades ONLY on a typed retryable LLMError (RATE_LIMIT/TIMEOUT/UNAVAILABLE); typed non-retryable and all untyped exceptions propagate (fail-closed). RouterExhaustedError (litellm) made a typed LLMError(kind=RATE_LIMIT) preserving its message keywords.
findings.regression_test: tests/unit/test_fallback_provider_law10.py (6 tests: 429-success, quota/rate-limit-success, typed-rate-limit-fallback, typed-timeout/unavailable-fallback, typed-non-retryable-propagates, untyped-exception-propagates)
findings.dependency: none (self-contained; no open PR #84-#91 touches fallback_provider.py or errors.py)
findings.notes: status becomes VERIFIED only after exact-SHA CI on this branch is green (LAW 16/17).

findings.domain: DATA / PRODUCTION (Wave B/J, death-condition 'production backup unverified')
findings.source_report: LIVE CI: maintenance schedule run 36115146739 failure on main
findings.precondition: Scheduled 'maintenance' workflow runs 'nexus maintenance backup' nightly; R2_* secrets must be configured for the GitHub Actions run.
findings.failure_scenario: Nightly production backup cannot run: create_backup() raises ProviderUnavailable and exits non-zero because R2 is not configured for the scheduled run. The job is red every night and NO verified production backup exists.
findings.reproduction: LIVE: gh run view 36115146739 -> backup-db step 'Run nexus maintenance backup' exit 1 (also 35975483186).
findings.root_cause: OPERATIONAL, not a code defect: backup.py is correctly fail-closed (task-167/P0-C). The scheduled GitHub Actions run lacks valid R2_ACCOUNT_ID/R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/R2_BUCKET secrets, so the backup hard-fails by design.
findings.fix: None applicable in code (behaviour is correct). Requires ops action: configure R2 secrets for the scheduled workflow (docs/ops/r2-storage.md), then a workflow_dispatch run must produce a green backup with sha256 + round-trip verification.
findings.regression_test: n/a (operational). Guard already exists: backup refuses to self-report success without artifact+sha256+integrity+round-trip.
findings.owner: ops / repo-admin (needs secret provisioning); engineering owner arena/01a0dc1e
findings.dependency: R2 credentials in GitHub Actions secrets + a verified workflow_dispatch backup run
findings.notes: Contributes to production NOT being verifiable. Fail-closed is correct; the gap is unproven production backup, recorded not forgotten (LAW 20).

findings.line: ~33 (temp cleanup runs before the dry_run guard; _clean_temp_dir unlinks)
findings.precondition: run_housekeeping(dry_run=True) is expected to perform zero filesystem mutation.

findings.fix: Gate temp cleanup on dry_run (return candidates only). OWNED by PR#90 (07106c29f8, green, DRAFT) and PR#91 (df533957ec).
